criteria.description: Cases are stratified into meaningful buckets (e.g. happy path, hard/edge, adversarial, should-refuse/out-of-scope) rather than one flat list.
Assigns a grader type (code/deterministic assertion, LLM-as-judge with a rubric, or human) appropriate to each quality dimension, rather than one generic score.
Where an LLM-as-judge or human grader is used, a written rubric or explicit criteria are specified — not just 'rate 1-10'.
Sets explicit pass/quality bars, ideally per bucket, including at least one zero-tolerance / hard-fail criterion for severe errors.
Recommends deriving failure modes / cases from real (or pilot) outputs rather than only imagined ones.
Mentions validating an LLM-as-judge against human labels, or otherwise checking grader trustworthiness.
Treats the eval set as living — production failures become new regression cases — and/or specifies a run cadence.
